answer: Each identity locks a 60-credit bond and files its work in a garden ledger, where each task becomes a key-signed timber entry. Each epoch, examiners ask three random questions from its timber entries, checked against crystal hashes. A mismatch burns the bond, and the proving examiner gets 20. One fake costs 60 plus 40 to invent history, or 100; 1,000 fakes cost 100,000, and the k-th fake pays 100, since a reused history burns both copies. A rented-history ring fails: rented answers cannot match details only the real worker knows. An honest agent locks 60 once and keeps it.
